rows.title: Attempt on Absence of infinite clusters at critical percolation
rows.body:
ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Critical branching-process extinction Result: For the regular tree at p=1/b, an infinite descendant cluster would have survival probability x satisfying x=1-(1-px)^b. For b>=2 strict concavity gives 1-(1-x/b)^b<x for every x>0, so only x=0 is possible. Check: The strict inequality can also be obtained from the binomial generating function lying strictly above its tangent at one. This excludes the deterministic b=1 exception, whose p_c is one. Obstruction: Critical clusters in a general quasi-transitive graph are not independent branching trees. Their loop dependence is not captured by this fixed-point proof.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-p0043-absence-of-infinite-clusters-at-critical-percolation

rows.title: Attempt on Conformal invariance of critical bond percolation on the square lattice
rows.body:
ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Look for a discrete holomorphic observable on the square lattice analogous to Smirnov's on the triangular lattice. Result: Smirnov's argument needs the three-arm colour-switching symmetry, which on the triangular lattice comes from site self-duality; on Z^2 bond percolation the dual is the shifted square lattice and the exploration interface lives on the medial lattice, where the parafermionic observable F(z) = E[e^{i sigma W(z)} 1_{z on interface}] with spin sigma = ... satisfies only half of the discrete Cauchy-Riemann relations (the contour-integral relations, as for FK models with q not 2). A concrete check: for the q=1 FK model the parafermionic observable has spin sigma = 2/3 and the relation sum over edges around a face vanishes, which gives crossing exponent bounds but not holomorphicity; the missing half is what conformal invariance needs. No new observable found. Obstruction: Only the weak (contour) half of discrete holomorphicity holds for the q=1 parafermion on the square lattice.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-c0017-conformal-invariance-of-critical-bond-percolation-on-the-square-lattic
No independent review; result status attempted_unsolved

rows.title: Attempt on Critical exponent beta = 1 in the asymptotic sense for high-dimensional percolation
rows.body:
ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Differentiate the magnetisation lace expansion at the critical point. Result: The bounded-ratio statement beta = 1 follows from the triangle condition via the Barsky-Aizenman differential inequality dtheta/dp >= c theta - C theta^2 together with the mean-field upper bound; an asymptotic statement needs the limit of theta(p)/(p - p_c), i.e. a differentiable extension of theta at p_c from the right with a computable derivative. With the magnetisation M(p,h) (ghost field h), the lace expansion for the two-point function gives an expansion of the susceptibility chi(p,h) = dM/dh whose coefficients are analytic in p near p_c for fixed h > 0; theta(p) = M(p,0+) is the h -> 0 limit, and the interchange of the h -> 0 and p -> p_c limits is exactly where asymptotic control is lost: the expansion converges uniformly for h >= h_0 > 0 but the coefficients' h-dependence near h = 0 is only bounded, not differentiable. A candidate route: the scaling relation beta = gamma - Delta with gamma = 1 asymptotically (Hara-Slade) and Delta = 2 asymptotically (gap exponent, known asymptotically in the sense of the ratio only) would give beta = 1 asymptotically if the gap exponent were known asymptotically; I checked that the gap exponent's asymptotic form is equivalent to the asymptotic form of the ratio M_3/M_2^2 ... in the source's notation, which is itself not derived. Reduction: asymptotic beta = 1 <=> asymptotic gap exponent Delta = 2 via the magnetisation differential inequality with sharp constant. Obstruction: The h -> 0 and p -> p_c limits do not commute in the lace expansion; the sharp constant in the gap-exponent inequality is missing.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-c0063-critical-exponent-beta-1-in-the-asymptotic-sense-for-high-dimensional
No independent review; result status attempted_unsolved

rows.title: Attempt on Exact critical percolation chemical-distance exponent
rows.body:
ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Exact critical percolation chemical-distance exponent structural reduction or obstruction Result: A shortest crossing may be chosen self-avoiding by deleting loops. Its length is at least a constant times R and at most the number of sites in the square, which is O(R^2). Thus any exponent defined by the stated expectation must lie in[1,2]. Check: The lower bound is net horizontal displacement divided by the maximum horizontal displacement per edge. The upper bound counts sites on a self-avoiding path, so it holds on every configuration with a crossing. Obstruction: These geometric bounds do not quantify the critical detours around closed clusters. Interface dimensions are not automatically dimensions of shortest open crossings.

rows.title: Attempt on Notions of criticality for percolation on high-dimensional tori
rows.body:
ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Compute the maximiser of d/dp log chi_T(p) in the mean-field random-graph analogue and compare with the window width. Result: For the Erdos-Renyi graph G(n, p) the susceptibility chi(p) = E|C(uniform vertex)| satisfies chi ~ 1/(1 - np) below the window and the derivative of log chi is maximised inside the critical window np = 1 + O(n^{-1/3}), at distance O(n^{-1/3}) from any other reasonable critical point; the same holds for the torus IF the torus susceptibility has the mean-field form chi_T(p) = chi_{Z^d}(p) + V (theta-like term) with the crossover at |p - p_c| ~ V^{-1/3}, which is the content of the torus plateau results (Theorem 13.9 of the source and the 2021 Hutchcroft-Michta-Slade torus plateau). Given the plateau, log chi_T is increasing with derivative of order 1/(p_c - p) below the window and of order V^{1/3} inside it, then decreasing above; so the maximiser lies within O(V^{-1/3}) of p_c(Z^d) provided the derivative inside the window is controlled from below, which requires the plateau statement with derivatives, i.e. a two-sided bound on d chi_T/dp inside the window. The plateau results bound chi_T itself, not its derivative; Russo's formula expresses the derivative as an expected number of pivotals, which in the window is of order chi_T times V^{1/3}, but only up to constants and only as an upper bound from the known results. Reduction: Open Problem 13.1 for p_c^{(1)} follows from a two-sided pivotal count inside the window. Obstruction: Two-sided derivative control of the torus susceptibility inside the scaling window is not available.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-c0067-notions-of-criticality-for-percolation-on-high-dimensional-tori
No independent review; result status attempted_unsolved

rows.title: Attempt on Scaling limit of critical percolation cluster sizes on the hypercube
rows.body:
ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Compare the exploration process of the hypercube with the Aldous exploration of the Erdos-Renyi graph. Result: Aldous's proof for G(n,p) uses that the exploration process is a random walk with drift theta - t and unit variance, up to depletion; on the hypercube the exploration of a cluster is a random walk whose step distribution depends on the local geometry (the number of unexplored neighbours of the current vertex is d minus the number of explored ones, and explored vertices are geometrically correlated). In the window the explored set has size V^{2/3} = 2^{2d/3}, which is a vanishing fraction of V, but the DEPLETION seen by a single vertex is not uniform: the explored vertices cluster geometrically, so the walk's drift correction is a functional of the geometry, not of the total explored mass as in G(n,p). This is exactly why the hypercube is harder than the Hamming graph (where the geometry is 'mean-field enough' and the scaling limit was obtained by Federico-van der Hofstad-den Hollander-Hulshof for the Hamming cube). A reduction: the scaling limit follows if the exploration's drift satisfies E[step | past] = theta 2^{-d/3} - (explored mass)/V + o(2^{-d/3}) uniformly over the window, i.e. if the local depletion is asymptotically equal to the global depletion; this is a 'non-backtracking randomness' statement about the geometry of critical hypercube clusters (that they are spread out like independent samples), which is the mean-field cluster geometry conjecture and is open. Obstruction: Local versus global depletion in the exploration walk; needs spread-out geometry of critical hypercube clusters.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-c0069-scaling-limit-of-critical-percolation-cluster-sizes-on-the-hypercube
No independent review; result status attempted_unsolved

rows.title: Attempt on Super-Brownian motion limit of critical percolation clusters in high dimensions
rows.body:
ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Identify gamma and v from known exponents and locate the missing joint convergence. Result: gamma = 1: the intrinsic one-arm probability is of order 1/n (Kozma-Nachmias), so n P_{p_c}(intrinsic radius >= n) is bounded, matching the canonical measure normalisation; v is the variance per intrinsic step of the spatial displacement, given by the lace expansion two-point function through the intrinsic-distance two-point function (C0079). The finite-dimensional distributions of the process in t are the intrinsic r-point functions with fixed intrinsic distances, which are the objects of C0079 (Open Problem 15.5) at the level of r = 2; the source's Theorem 15.4 handles the number-of-pivotals two-point function, and the intrinsic distance version is the missing step. Given the intrinsic r-point functions, convergence of finite-dimensional distributions to SBM follows as in the oriented case (Hofstad-Slade), and tightness follows from the one-arm bound and a modulus-of-continuity estimate for the intrinsic exploration. So the problem reduces to Open Problem 15.5 extended to r-point functions. Obstruction: Intrinsic-distance r-point functions not lace-expanded for unoriented percolation.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-c0076-super-brownian-motion-limit-of-critical-percolation-clusters-in-high-d

rows.title: Attempt on Uniqueness-critical percolation versus invariant spanning trees
rows.body:
ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Conditional implication through the component-bijection conjecture Result: If there is no invariant random spanning tree, the invariant FMSF cannot be connected, because a connected spanning forest would itself be such a tree. If the stronger conjecture in P0055 gave a bijection between free-forest components and infinite p_u clusters, that disconnection would imply multiple clusters at p_u. Check: The first implication uses only the definition of an invariant spanning tree. The second is explicitly conditional on a separate unproved component correspondence. Obstruction: Two properties sharing FMSF disconnection as a consequence do not thereby imply one another. Neither unconditional implication in the source question is established here.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-p0057-uniqueness-critical-percolation-versus-invariant-spanning-trees

This is the input that the 2026 barrier-breaking paper consumes.
rows.body:
rotationally invariant first passage percolation on the plane
the authors describe the hypotheses only as ones 'which can be verified for many standard rotationally invariant models of first passage percolation, e.g. Riemannian FPP, Voronoi FPP and the Howard-Newman model' - the hypothesis SET itself is not available to lane P4

WHY THE STATUS IS abstract-only AND NOT MORE: the abstract names the conclusion and the model class but deliberately abstracts the hypotheses behind 'hypotheses which can be verified for many standard rotationally invariant models'. Since the whole question for the campaign is WHICH hypotheses are load-bearing and whether any lattice analogue could satisfy them, an abstract that does not list them is not enough to answer anything. Anyone who needs the dependency audit of the 2026 paper has to read this one.

rows.title: Bernoulli Percolation, theta(p), and the Critical Probability
rows.body: In BOND percolation on a graph G with parameter p in [0,1], each edge is declared open with probability p and closed otherwise, independently; P_p denotes the resulting product measure on {0,1}^{E(G)}. The open cluster C(x) of a vertex x is the set of vertices reachable from x through open edges. Write theta(p) = P_p( |C(0)| = infinity ) for a fixed origin. Coupling all parameters on a common family of independent uniform variables - edge e open at level p exactly when U_e <= p - shows theta is nondecreasing, so the CRITICAL PROBABILITY p_c(G) = sup{ p : theta(p) = 0 } = inf{ p : theta(p) > 0 } is well defined. SITE percolation is defined analogously with vertices; the two have different critical values on the same graph, and p_c^{bond} <= p_c^{site} on any graph. On Z^d with d >= 2 one has 0 < p_c < 1, with the explicit elementary bounds 1/(2d-1) <= p_c^{bond}(Z^d) < 1. The value is known exactly only in special cases, most famously p_c^{bond}(Z^2) = 1/2. Whether theta(p_c) = 0 in every dimension is a celebrated open problem: it is known for d = 2 (Harris and Kesten) and, by lace-expansion methods, in high dimensions - Hara and Slade for large d, later reduced to d >= 11 by Fitzner and van der Hofstad - and it was still open for the intermediate dimensions 3 <= d <= 10 at the time this node was written. [standard; e.g. Grimmett, Percolation, 2nd ed., Chapters 1 and 8]

The open cluster C(x) of a vertex x is the set of vertices reachable from x through open edges. Write theta(p) = P_p( |C(0)| = infinity ) for a fixed origin. Coupling all parameters on a common family of independent uniform variables - edge e open at level p exactly when U_e <= p - shows theta is nondecreasing, so the CRITICAL PROBABILITY p_c(G) = sup{ p : theta(p) = 0 } = inf{ p : theta(p) > 0 } is well defined. SITE percolation is defined analogously with vertices; the two have different critical values on the same graph, and p_c^{bond} <= p_c^{site} on any graph. On Z^d with d >= 2 one has 0 < p_c < 1, with the explicit elementary bounds 1/(2d-1) <= p_c^{bond}(Z^d) < 1. The value is known exactly only in special cases, most famously p_c^{bond}(Z^2) = 1/2. Whether theta(p_c) = 0 in every dimension is a celebrated open problem: it is known for d = 2 (Harris and Kesten) and, by lace-expansion methods, in high dimensions - Hara and Slade for large d, later reduced to d >= 11 by Fitzner and van der Hofstad - and it was still open for the intermediate dimensions 3 <= d <= 10 at the time this node was written. [standard; e.g. Grimmett, Percolation, 2nd ed., Chapters 1 and 8]","status":"unverified"}

rows.title: Critical percolation clusters on the torus wrap around it exactly when d > 6, which is the mechanism behind mean-field (Erdos-Renyi-like) depletion
rows.body:
PRIVATE MECHANISM NOTE, author-recorded. On the torus T_{n,d} with volume V, a critical cluster of size V^{2/3} has intrinsic geometry of a critical tree embedded four-dimensionally, so its Euclidean diameter is of order (V^{2/3})^{1/4} = V^{1/6}, while the torus side is V^{1/d}. Since V^{1/6} > V^{1/d} iff d > 6, above six dimensions the window clusters wrap around the torus many times and see the torus uniformly; this is why the exploration process should have the same global (mass-proportional) depletion as in G(n,p), which is what the multiplicative-coalescent scaling limit (Heydenreich-van der Hofstad Open Problems 13.3 and 13.5) needs. The torus plateau theorem (Hutchcroft-Michta-Slade) is the two-point version of this uniformity; the open step is the exploration-level (higher-point) version. Same reason makes eps >> V^{-1/3} lie above the correlation-length crossover eps >> V^{-2/d} for d > 6 (Open Problem 13.2).
Bernoulli percolation on the discrete torus, d > 6
Mean-field cluster geometry (intrinsic diameter m^{1/2}, Euclidean diameter m^{1/4})

rows.title: Damron-Houdre-Ozdemir (2022): a POLYNOMIAL fluctuation lower bound does exist in planar first-passage percolation, but for a different observable - T_n, the minimal passage time between two opposite sides of an n by n square - under a curvature assumption and for exponentially distributed weights, where the fluctuations of T_n are at least of order n^{1/8-epsilon} for every epsilon > 0. This is NOT a bound on the point-to-point passage time T(0,x), where the best lower bound is still logarithmic.
rows.body:
the observable is T_n, the minimal passage time between two opposite sides of an n by n square - a minimum over crossings, not a point-to-point passage time
a curvature assumption on the limit shape (unproven in first-passage percolation)
the edge weights t_e are exponentially distributed
d = 2

WHY A SEPARATE ARGUMENT WAS NEEDED, in the authors' words: 'previous arguments to bound the fluctuations of T(x,y) only give a constant lower bound for those of T_n (even assuming curvature)', so they represent T_n as a minimum of cylinder passage times and use the Markov property to get finer distributional information. The minimum-over-crossings structure is the whole difficulty and the whole difference.
COROLLARY they state: the first polynomial lower bounds on higher central moments of the discrete torus passage time, under the same curvature assumption.
THE MISQUOTE THIS NODE EXISTS TO BLOCK: 'polynomial variance lower bounds are known in FPP'. They are known for this observable, under an unproven curvature assumption, for one weight law (extended by Dembin-Elboim to absolutely continuous laws). Nothing polynomial is known unconditionally for Var T(0,x).
SOURCE: arXiv:2204.06592v1, 'Fluctuation bounds for first-passage percolation on the square, tube, and torus'. Official arXiv API record retrieved by lane P4 on 2026-08-22.
VERIFICATION STATUS: theorem-checked-against-source. The abstract states the observable, the curvature hypothesis, the weight law and the exponent; the proof was not read.
